### 1 — Scene
A mixed dinner plate: sliced grilled beef, yellow couscous or a similar fine grain, cooked squash/zucchini, and a creamy dressed green salad with croutons and grated cheese.

### 2 — Vessel
A square dinner plate, roughly 26–28 cm across. Allowing for its rounded corners and rim, I’ll use an effective diameter of **26 cm**:
**Area = 3.14 × 13² ≈ 530 cm².**

### 3–7 — Items, area, volume, weight and energy
Areas below are approximate non-overlapping allocations; dressing and cheese occupy parts of the salad’s footprint.

| Visible item | Plate area | Area × height = gross volume | Density | Weight | kcal/100 g | kcal |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Salad greens | 21% | 111 × 2.5 = 278 ml | 0.18 | 50 g | 20 | 10 |
| Creamy dressing | 2% | 11 × 0.9 = 10 ml | 1.0 | 10 g | 450 | 45 |
| Croutons | 3% | 16 × 1.0 = 16 ml | 0.5 | 8 g | 410 | 33 |
| Grated cheese | 1% | 5 × 0.3 = 1.5 ml | 0.9 | 2 g | 400 | 8 |
| Yellow couscous/grain mixture | 23% | 122 × 1.7 = 207 ml | 0.8 | 166 g | 150 | 249 |
| Grilled beef strips | 13% | 69 × 1.2 = 83 ml | 0.95 | 79 g | 240 | 190 |
| Cooked yellow squash and zucchini | 14% | 74 × 2.0 = 148 ml | 0.6 | 89 g | 45 | 40 |

The vegetable and grain energy estimates allow for light cooking fat; no separate pool of oil is visible.

### 8 — Sanity check
The allocated areas total **77% of the plate**, consistent with the visible coverage. Estimated total: **404 g and 575 kcal**. This is plausible for the moderate grain portion, several beef strips, vegetables and salad. Portion depth and cooking fat are the largest uncertainties.
